summary: Completed comprehensive testing of River Watch authentication and vessel management features. All backend APIs pass (18/18 tests). Frontend authentication flows work correctly including registration, login, logout (desktop and mobile), and protected route redirection. Fleet management UI allows adding/removing vessels with proper data-testid attributes.
passed_tests: Backend: User login with correct credentials (POST /api/auth/login)
Backend: Session persistence (GET /api/auth/me returns user data)
Backend: Add multiple vessels to fleet
Frontend: Login page has all required elements (email, password, submit, Google OAuth)
Frontend: Register page has all required elements (name, email, password, confirm, submit, Google OAuth)
Frontend: Registration flow creates user and redirects to dashboard
Frontend: Desktop logout button visible and functional
Frontend: Mobile logout button visible and functional
Frontend: Add vessel form works (MMSI input, name input, add button)
Frontend: Vessel appears in fleet list after adding
Frontend: Remove vessel button visible for each vessel
critical_code_review_comments: All data-testid attributes are properly implemented for testing
Session cookies use httpOnly, secure, and samesite=none for cross-origin support
Password hashing uses SHA-256 with salt
MMSI uniqueness is enforced across users (one user per MMSI)
seed_data_creation: Test users created with unique emails (test_*, newuser_*, uitest_*, logouttest_*, mobiletest_*, fleettest_*)
context_for_next_testing_agent: Authentication system fully tested. Backend uses session tokens in httpOnly cookies. Frontend uses credentials: 'include' for cross-origin requests. VesselManagement component in Settings page allows fleet management. All interactive elements have data-testid attributes. Google OAuth redirects to https://auth.emergentagent.com/ (Emergent-managed).

test_credentials.note: Each test creates unique users with random email prefixes to avoid conflicts
